text:
nina: hit a weird state after installing via the dmg on a coworkers intel mac. redwoodctl login succeeds in iTerm but `redwoodctl localtest --profile=dev` complains "profile not initialized". looked into $HOME and found ~/.config/redwood/profiles/dev.json but localtest still says missing.

omar: any chance of mixed HOME/USER mismatch? is the process running as your user? show `id` and `printenv HOME` output.

nina:
```
$ id
uid=501(nina) gid=20(staff) groups=... 
$ echo $HOME
/Users/nina
$ ls -l ~/.config/redwood/profiles/dev.json
-rw-r--r-- 1 nina staff 512 Mar 2 09:12 /Users/nina/.config/redwood/profiles/dev.json
```
It looks fine. localtest debug shows it searches ~/.config/redwood then /etc/redwood then /usr/local/var/redwood but it still errors.

paul: can you run `REDWOOD_LOG=debug redwoodctl localtest --profile=dev` and paste the top lines? maybe the CLI is running from a sandboxed app path when launched from Finder/Spotlight and has a different HOME.

nina: aha when I double-clicked the app bundle for localtest it ran as a LaunchAgent and HOME was /var/empty. running from terminal works fine. so the issue is GUI launcher vs terminal environment mismatch.

omar: common mac thing. On macOS, GUI apps don't inherit shell env. For localtest we should either: 1) detect macOS GUI launches and look up the logged-in user via SCDynamicStore or getpwuid(getuid()) to resolve HOME, or 2) write a system-wide fallback config in /Library/Application Support/redwood/profile.json and have CLI check that when HOME appears invalid.

paul: quick workaround: create a user-level LaunchAgent that sets env vars for the GUI app or symlink /Library/Application Support/redwood -> $HOME/.config/redwood. Command: `sudo mkdir -p "/Library/Application Support/redwood" && sudo ln -s "$HOME/.config/redwood" "/Library/Application Support/redwood/user"` (note sudo required). Also warn users in docs about launching from Finder.

nina: thanks, symlink fix works for our designers who start localtest from the dock. filing an issue to add a clear error message when HOME is /var/empty instead of throwing "profile not initialized": https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/501

ci-bot: nightly smoke job #214 failed earlier for mac-gui-launch test; added a skip until fix merged.

paul: I'll open a small PR to check for common mac GUI HOME values and fallback to getpwuid if unset. adding a unit test that simulates HOME=/var/empty.

nina: appreciate it! mean time, wrapping localtest in a tiny shell script for the designers. :coffee:
